newsitem.title: USA: Clinton proposes $300 mln authority to aid D.C..
newsitem.headline: Clinton proposes $300 mln authority to aid D.C..

text.p: President Clinton on Tuesday called for a new nine-member authority armed with $300 million in grants and tax incentives to spur economic development in the financially troubled District of Columbia.

The proposed Economic Development Corporation would get an initial, one-time financing of $50 million to set up shop and $250 million in tax incentives to encourage business investment downtown and in distressed D.C. communities, Clinton said at a White House press briefing.

"(This) city is every American's home and should be every American's pride," Clinton said. "We must help our capital city lift itself to a point where it can be model for revitalization. Now is the time."

Clinton said the new non-federal public-private corporation would develop a development strategy for the city, coordinate large-scale projects, help create jobs for low-income city residents, and connect D.C. development to that of the region.
